audited_by: ep31 render worker (two fresh readers, third reader compared old/new)

faults.what: The person seated at the right of the table has no head or neck: a dark bottle-shaped lump sits on the shoulders of a grey vest with a pink sleeved arm below it.
Teddy is a young clean-shaven man with thick dark hair in a teal top, not the thin unshaven man in his fifties in a faded blue shirt of k35 and k56.
faults.where: left, the man over the bowl

faults.what: The opening family are generic strangers: no topknot on Indio, no white-haired Tala, and an old man in place of Lola in her flowered dress.
Eight generic people laugh round the table, one of them a blonde woman; none of Indio, Lola, Tala, Teddy or Liwayway is recognisable.
The five people in blankets on the roof are strangers drawn large and in focus: no topknot, no white hair, no grandmother, no dog.
Tala has long brown hair and warm brown eyes in both close-ups instead of snow-white hair and pale silver eyes (reader 1's k15 does not belong here; see refuted).
faults.where: the young woman's face and hair

faults.what: Lola is a short grey-haired woman in a plaid shirt and dark vest, not the bun and flowered house dress she wears in k09 and k33, and a grey-haired middle-aged man sits where white-haired Tala should be.
Usman's eyes are bulging yellow rings with pin-dot pupils and his muzzle carries a human-like row of teeth, so the close-up looks deranged; his fur is brown, not black.
faults.where: dog's eyes and mouth, middle of frame

faults.what: Usman is drawn as a long-muzzled Labrador with two floppy ears and brown eyes, and the red kerchief is missing.
Three large kana-like characters are painted along the building fascia at the top right.
Usman has two tall pointed ears and a wolfish head filling the frame, not one folded ear.
Usman never has one folded ear: both ears hang down in k18, k38, k67 and k73 and both stand up in k72, so his head changes breed from shot to shot.
Pale blue signature-like letter marks are painted on the water at the bottom right.
Green leaves and a flower from Lola's dress print are drawn on the bare skin of her hand and wrist.

The close-up hand has a thumb and only three fingers, one of them tipless; the box is open, empty and lying on top of the jeans instead of in the pocket, and the torso above the waistband is bare skin, not the grey t-shirt.
Liwayway's raised hand has fingers fused at the base that split into extra tips, with a further finger entering from the right edge, so the count reads as six.
faults.where: right of middle, her raised hand

faults.what: The dagger's tip and handle are each clamped in metal strap-and-buckle gadgets fitted with a red and orange jewelled eye and strapped round a furry limb; no hand holds it and no rope is being cut.
Indio is drawn as a young boy with a bowl haircut, a cream shirt, no topknot and no red handkerchief.
The billboard that should be blank carries three advert panels full of fake lettering.
Both of Indio's hands are mitten blobs with no separate fingers, the left one smeared with a brown lump, and the red handkerchief hangs out of his jeans pocket instead of being tied on his wrist.
M's hand at the top left has long boneless tapering fingers with a spike of a thumb (they do not in fact touch Indio's hand, which is sound).
faults.where: upper left of the crop, her hand on the blanket

faults.what: At the bottom right two hands of different skin tones run into each other round a black hole where the fingers should be, and the lower hand at the bottom left has lumps instead of fingers.
The billboard carries a poster of two anime faces over a strip of fake lettering instead of being blank.
A paper notice pinned to the kitchen wall carries a heading and five lines of fake text.
Letter-like marks sit on the fascia over the doorway at the far end of the street.
A hanging shop sign on the left carries red letter-like marks.
The fascia of the school building carries a row of red letter-like marks.
A white banner over the hall doors carries two rows of red fake lettering across a third of the frame width.
The hologram shows a percent sign after the bar (and a question mark in place of the shepherd's crook).
Seen from behind, Usman's white chest patch is painted on his back and rump instead of his chest.
Indio holds a modern black camera zoom lens, with moulded maker's letters on the barrel, instead of the round gold-rimmed lens he raises in k47.
The six at the closing meal are all children and teenagers; no Lola, no topknot, none of the cast.

Usman's open mouth is a straight human-like row of small square white teeth and his eyes have white sclera with human brows, so the dog looks like a man in a dog suit; the red kerchief is worn as a hood over the top of his head.

M is a brown-haired young woman in a pale blue top standing over the table with her head cut off above the mouth: no long black hair, no long dark coat, and she is not in the doorway the shot calls for.
In this extreme close-up Indio has a heavy square jaw, thick neck and a swept-back pompadour with no topknot, reading as an older, bigger man than the lean youth of k47 and k71.

The named character the shot is built on is simply absent: k10 and k12 are empty kitchens where Lola's and Tala's close-ups should be, k16 shows Lola alone with no M to pull in, k32 shows Indio alone with no Lola to lift, k35 shows Teddy alone with no Tala and no neighbours.
Moulded maker's letters and numbers run along the barrel of the black lens.

third_reader.notes: laugh_rain (Indio twice), rooftop_all (4 people, grandmother twice) and punyal_cut (second hand, blade missing the rope) were reworded and redrawn once more; the new versions show 5 people, 5 people in a row, and one hand cutting the rope, checked at 3x
